rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide/lecture headers pass the squint test AND the truth clause
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm the rule prevents: a header that names nothing (empty container) or asserts more than the body supports (a lie dressed as a header). This file is slide-format per its own STATUS line and renders as 3 slides (confirmed below). Squint: 'Checking can cost far less than doing' (line 3), 'Why this decides what to delegate' (line 9), 'Every send-off needs a named cheap verifier' (line 15) each name a claim, not an empty container ('The move', 'The question') or orphan mystery. No two headers duplicate. Truth clause -- closest-to-violating line is header 3's universal 'Every send-off needs...': body licenses it by covering both branches exhaustively ('Before a send-off, ask: what is my cheap verifier here?... If you can name one, the task is a delegation candidate. No cheap verifier? Two options. Keep the task, or build the verifier first and then delegate.') -- the universal is a stated discipline the section fully supports, not an overclaim.
